rows.note: Use 波浪 as the default noun for a water wave, and also for a clearly wavy shape such as in hair.

example.jyutping: ni1 go3 bo1 long6 hou2 daai6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for waving your hand in greeting or goodbye, including a farewell signal.

example.english: I wave to him when I leave.
example.jyutping: ngo5 zau2 go2 zan6 tung4 keoi5 fai1 sau2

rows.note: Use this when the wave is specifically meant to beckon someone or call their attention.

example.english: I wave to call him over when I see him.
example.traditional: 我見到佢就招手叫佢過嚟。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gin3 dou2 keoi5 zau6 ziu1 sau2 giu3 keoi5 gwo3 lei4

rows.note: Use this for something moving loosely back and forth, such as a flag moving in the breeze.

example.english: When the wind blows, the flag will wave.
example.jyutping: fung1 jat1 ceoi1 kei4 zau6 jiu4

rows.note: Use 潮流 for a movement or trend in popular culture or fashion.

example.english: This fashion wave has brought wide-leg trousers back.
example.traditional: 呢股潮流令闊腳褲翻生喇。
example.jyutping: ni1 gu2 ciu4 lau4 ling6 fut3 goek3 fu3 faan1 saang1 laa3

rows.note: Use 人潮 when the sudden surge consists of a crowd of people, especially shoppers or passengers.

example.english: As soon as work lets out, a wave of people pours into the mall.
example.traditional: 放工時間一到，人潮就湧入商場。
example.jyutping: fong3 gung1 si4 gaan3 jat1 dou3 jan4 ciu4 zau6 jung2 jap6 soeng1 coeng4

rows.note: Use this when something floats or wafts along like a wave, such as shadows or mist.

example.english: The mist on the mountain slowly moves like a wave.
example.jyutping: saan1 soeng6 di1 mou6 maan6 maan6 piu1 dung6

rows.note: Use 手勢 for the hand gesture itself when someone waves to signal, dismiss, or attract attention.

example.english: They used a hand gesture to wave me over.
example.jyutping: keoi5 jung6 sau2 sai3 giu3 ngo5 gwo3 heoi3
